title: Knowledge Check 8 - Lessons 36-41
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 36-41 - Predictive and Generative AI. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A consultant is asked why an Agentforce sales agent replied with a price that is three quarters old. Which root cause fits how the platform works?
options: The topic description was too broad
The agent's grounding retrieved a stale price book record, so the answer can only be as current as the source data
The reasoning engine needs a larger language model
The agent needs more actions attached to the topic
questions.explanation: The agent composes from what grounding retrieves, so a stale source produces a stale answer. Swapping the model or adding actions does nothing about the age of the retrieved record.

questions.question: A sales org wants the agent to check order status in an external ERP and then draft a follow up email. What must the consultant configure?
options: Only a larger prompt template
Only a Data Cloud data stream
An action that reaches the ERP through a Flow or an Apex invocable method, attached to the relevant topic, plus a prompt template or action for the draft
A new permission set on the Opportunity object
questions.explanation: The agent can only run actions you attach, so reaching the ERP requires an action, and the drafting step is satisfied by a prompt template or another action. A data stream alone gives the agent nothing to run.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes topic selection at run time?
options: The Atlas Reasoning Engine picks the topic whose scope best matches the request and then selects an action within it
The user must name the topic before the agent responds
Topics run in creation order until one succeeds
Every topic runs on every request and the agent merges the results
questions.explanation: The reasoning engine classifies the request against topic scope and then chooses an action from that topic's action list. The other options describe scripted behavior the platform does not use.

questions.question: A sales team wants a summary of an Opportunity written into a field on the record whenever the rep asks, with no conversation involved. Which tool fits?
options: An Agentforce agent with one topic per summary
Einstein Conversation Insights
A prompt template of the Record Summary type, grounded on the Opportunity and its related records
Einstein Opportunity Scoring
questions.explanation: A single grounded generation with known inputs is a prompt template job of the Record Summary type, not an agent or a scoring feature.

questions.question: A regulated customer insists their prompt text and the model's completions are never stored by the model provider and never reused for training. Which Salesforce mechanism answers this?
options: The Einstein Trust Layer's zero data retention with the model provider, working alongside masking and the audit trail
A sharing rule on the prompt object
Turning off Einstein Activity Capture
A validation rule on the record
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is the Trust Layer control that governs whether the provider stores or reuses the prompt and response, and masking and audit work with it. The other options do not touch what the provider does with the data.

questions.question: A customer wants inference to run on a model they already host with a specific provider for regional reasons. What does the consultant configure?
options: A new Data Cloud data stream
An Apex callout from a trigger
A custom Lightning component
A bring your own model connection registered in Model Builder and then selected on the prompt template or agent
questions.explanation: Model Builder is where you register an external provider model and make it selectable for prompts and agents, and the Trust Layer still applies to the call.

questions.question: An org has 240 closed won and 180 closed lost opportunities in the last 24 months. What does Einstein Opportunity Scoring do?
options: Scores every record with a local model
Displays no scores at all
Scores only the closed won opportunities
Builds no local model yet and falls back to a global model because the closed lost requirement is not met
questions.explanation: The requirement is 200 closed won and 200 closed lost in the last 24 months, so the closed lost shortfall means no local model and a fallback to the global model.

questions.question: Which statement about Einstein Lead Scoring data requirements is correct?
options: 200 converted leads in the last 24 months
At least 1,000 leads created in the last 200 days with at least 120 converted to an account and contact
1,000 converted leads in the last 12 months
No minimum, because the global model always applies
questions.explanation: Lead Scoring needs 1,000 leads created in the last 200 days and at least 120 converted, which is a different threshold set from Opportunity Scoring.

questions.question: A sales leader asks how often the Opportunity Score on an open deal changes.
options: Opportunity scores are updated every few hours while the model itself is reanalyzed roughly monthly or when settings change
Scores are static once assigned
Scores refresh only during month end forecasting
Scores update once every 30 days
questions.explanation: Scores refresh every few hours and the underlying model is reanalyzed on a roughly monthly cadence or when an admin updates the settings.

questions.question: A sales VP wants the system to tell reps which single action to take next on an at risk renewal, not just a probability. Which capability answers the requirement?
options: Einstein Lead Scoring
An Einstein Next Best Action strategy built in Flow on top of a prediction
Einstein Activity Capture
A validation rule on the Opportunity
questions.explanation: A recommendation is produced by a strategy layer that converts a prediction into an action, which is what Einstein Next Best Action does. A score or a sync feature does not produce advice.

questions.question: A consultant needs a prediction for renewal likelihood, a target with no shipped scorer, and the sales leaders want to see which factors drive it. What fits?
options: Enable Einstein Lead Scoring on the Account object
Use Opportunity Score as a proxy
Build a report with a formula field
Build an Einstein Discovery story and model on a dataset with renewal as the outcome, then deploy the prediction field
questions.explanation: Einstein Discovery builds a model for a target of your choosing and surfaces the drivers, which is exactly what a custom outcome with an explanation requirement needs.

questions.question: A manager asks what unlocks coaching evidence from recorded sales calls, including talk ratio and competitor mentions.
options: Einstein Activity Capture
Opportunity Scoring factors
Einstein Conversation Insights, deployed alongside a recording consent process
A prompt template in Prompt Builder
questions.explanation: Conversation Insights records and transcribes calls and surfaces talk ratios and competitor mentions, and recording consent has to be handled wherever it is deployed.

questions.question: An org enables a lead scoring model and finds that reps now contact almost only the segment they always contacted, while a previously unworked segment is never surfaced. What is the correct diagnosis?
options: The model needs a larger dataset
Einstein Activity Capture is broken
The model has learned the historical contact pattern and is reinforcing it, a bias and feedback loop problem, so the segment criteria and field set need review
The lead scores simply need refreshing more often
questions.explanation: The model reproduces the historical working pattern and the business follows it, which is a feedback loop created by biased training history, not a data volume or sync defect.

questions.question: A field holding a customer's postal code is included in a scoring model and correlates strongly with a protected characteristic in that region. What should the consultant do?
options: Evaluate the field as a proxy, consider excluding it, and monitor outcome distribution by segment
Keep it because it improves accuracy
Encrypt the field
Move the field to a different object
questions.explanation: A strong proxy behaves like a protected attribute, so the control is to evaluate exclusion and then watch outcomes by segment. Encrypting or relocating the field leaves the correlation intact.

questions.question: A consultant is preparing to enable call recording insights in a region with strict consent rules. What is the first step?
options: Enable the feature and disclose at a later date
Confirm the consent and disclosure process meets the local requirement before enabling, since recording conversations is legally constrained
Rely on the Einstein Trust Layer to handle consent
Ask individual users to opt out
questions.explanation: Recording consent is a legal prerequisite that the platform does not obtain for you, so it is confirmed before the feature is enabled for a team.

questions.question: A customer's security team asks which Salesforce mechanism means their prompt text and the model's answer are not stored by a third party model provider.
options: The Einstein Trust Layer's zero data retention with the model provider, working with masking and the audit trail
A sharing rule on the prompt template
Disabling Einstein Activity Capture
Storing the model in a sandbox
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is the Trust Layer control that governs provider storage and reuse of prompts and completions, and it operates alongside masking and the audit trail.

questions.question: A regulator asks how the org ensures its lead scoring does not systematically exclude a customer group. Which principle is at stake and what is the control?
options: Transparency, so publish the model weights
Security, so encrypt the score field
Inclusivity, with outcome monitoring by segment and a named owner accountable for the result
Reliability, by refreshing scores more often
questions.explanation: Systematic exclusion is an inclusivity and accountability question, and the control is monitoring outcomes by segment with someone answerable for the finding.

questions.question: Which principle is served when Salesforce applies data masking so sensitive field values are replaced before a prompt leaves the org?
options: Honesty
Inclusivity
Accuracy
Privacy and security, since masking limits what personal data leaves the platform
questions.explanation: Masking keeps sensitive values from leaving Salesforce, which is the privacy and security duty rather than a grounding or tone concern.
